title: spec review: Q12: orchestrator/jev_planner.py — Jev as a shadow routing signal for Planner tier choice: typed batched questions over redacted structured state, fail open, never bypasses hard escalation (P12)
spec:
Why: the brief (P12) allows Jev to provide probabilistic decision characteristics to the Planner router, shadow first, as a signal and never as authority. jev_points.py (T-0586) already shows the pattern: typed options, redacted evidence, mode per point, fail open. Nothing asks Jev about Planner routing.
What: new module orchestrator/jev_planner.py; jev.ask injected as ask_fn so tests never hit the network.
- QUESTIONS = OrderedDict of five typed yes/no questions keyed routine_localized, architectural_reasoning, requirements_ambiguous, long_horizon, fable_improves_outcome, each with a one-sentence text.
- state(classification, ctx, goal) -> bounded redacted dict: decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, risk_class, signals (cap 10), goal_title (jev.redact, cap 200), spec_excerpt (jev.redact of the first 300 chars of goal spec), scope_count, scout_count, failing_test_count, spec_review_request_changes, auto_fix_rounds_used, signature_repeated. Never file contents, never diffs, never review comment bodies; total json <= 4000 chars (truncate spec_excerpt first).
- should_ask(router_mode, jev_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route) -> (bool, reason): False with reasons jev_off (jev_mode off), hard_decision (hard_reasons non-empty), single_tier (fewer than two available tiers in availability), deterministic (route.name != "escalate"), cannot_affect (router_mode == "off"); True otherwise (shadow and active both ask; in shadow the router records but does not apply — the router's responsibility, documented here).
- ask(classification, ctx, goal, *, cfg, router_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route, ask_fn=jev.ask, cache=None, root=None) -> {"asked": bool, "reason", "mode": jev_mode, "signals": {key: p or None}, "soft_adjust": float, "confidence": float|None, "cached": bool}. One ask_fn call carrying all five questions (batched). soft_adjust = clamp(0.2 * (p_architectural + p_ambiguous + p_long_horizon + p_fable_improves)/4 - 0.2 * p_routine, -0.2, 0.2); any missing/malformed/None answer -> soft_adjust 0.0 with reason jev_unavailable or jev_malformed. cache: dict keyed (goal_id, state_version from ctx.get("state_version"), decision_type) -> result, hit sets cached True and skips ask_fn. Every call (asked or skipped) appends a row via schedlog.append("planner_jev", {...state summary fields, asked, reason, signals, soft_adjust, mode}) without the question text bodies.
- Timeouts: ask_fn returning None (jev.ask's fail-open contract) -> asked True, reason jev_unavailable, soft_adjust 0.0.
- summary(root=None) -> {"n", "asked", "skip_reasons": Counter dict, "mean_soft_adjust"} tolerant of malformed lines.
acceptance: tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_off_and_hard_and_single_tier_never_ask — jev_mode off, hard_reasons ['security'], one available tier and a routine route each give asked False with the documented reason and no ask_fn call

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_batched_single_call_and_soft_adjust_bounds — one ask_fn call carries five questions; answers p=1.0 for architectural/ambiguous/long_horizon/fable and 0 routine give soft_adjust 0.2; all routine gives -0.2; never outside [-0.2, 0.2]

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_malformed_and_timeout_fail_open — ask_fn returning None and ask_fn returning {'answers': 'garbage'} both yield soft_adjust 0.0 with reasons jev_unavailable / jev_malformed, and a row is still recorded

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_state_is_redacted_and_bounded — a goal spec with a token-like secret and 20k chars yields state with spec_excerpt <= 300 chars, redacted by jev.redact, no key named diff/contents/comments, json <= 4000 chars

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_cache_hit_skips_network_and_summary_counts — second ask with the same (goal, state_version, decision_type) returns cached True with zero extra ask_fn calls; summary counts asked and skip reasons over rows including one malformed line

risks.issue: state(classification, ctx, goal) must derive decision_type/band/architectural/risk_class/signals from `classification`, but nothing in the spec or codebase defines that object's shape. decision.Route (orchestrator/decision.py:26) only carries name/reason/evidence/cheaper_steps/tier, and build_ctx's ctx (orchestrator/planner_runs.py:1002) carries task_class but no band/architectural/risk_class. No acceptance test pins these fields' contents (test_state_is_redacted_and_bounded only checks spec_excerpt/redaction/size), so an executor can invent any structure and every test still passes, deferring the real mismatch to the future wiring task.

The cache key is (goal_id, state_version from ctx.get('state_version'), decision_type), but build_ctx (orchestrator/planner_runs.py:1002-1020) never sets ctx['state_version'] -- it's tracked separately via state_version(goal_id) at launch time (orchestrator/planner_runs.py:939). Without an explicit instruction to inject it, every real call keys on None and the cache degenerates to a single bucket per (goal_id, decision_type).

state()'s 'signals (cap 10)' has no named source collection (not ctx, not goal, not classification per the other bullets), so it's unclear what upstream list/dict gets truncated and redacted -- risk of an executor passing through an under-redacted structure since no test exercises this field.

Acceptance only specifies that a cache hit skips ask_fn and returns cached True; it doesn't say whether a schedlog row is still appended on a hit. If it isn't, summary()'s 'asked' count will undercount real shadow activity; if it is, the row's 'cached' flag needs to be asserted somewhere.

suggested_spec_changes: Name the exact producer and field contract for `classification` (or drop it and derive decision_type/band/architectural/risk_class straight from `route` and `ctx`, which are already grounded in decision.py/build_ctx)
State explicitly that callers must set ctx['state_version'] (e.g. via planner_runs.state_version(goal_id)) before calling ask(), since build_ctx does not populate it today
Name the source collection for the capped 'signals' list in state() so its redaction/bounding is testable
Clarify whether schedlog.append fires on a cache hit and add an assertion for it in test_cache_hit_skips_network_and_summary_counts
